questions.q: What does the colon syntax, e.g. raw_payload:ticket_id, do?
options: Reaches into the VARIANT value and returns one named field, still typed VARIANT
Deletes the field from the VARIANT value
Converts the whole row to a string
Runs a stored procedure named ticket_id
questions.explain: The colon operator extracts a named field from a VARIANT value, but the result is still VARIANT-typed until explicitly cast.

questions.q: What does the double-colon in raw_payload:refund_amount::NUMBER(10,2) do?
options: Casts the extracted value to an explicit SQL type
Extracts a second field from the JSON
Rounds the value to the nearest integer
Marks the field as required (not nullable)
questions.explain: :: casts the extracted VARIANT value to a real SQL type, such as NUMBER(10,2) or TIMESTAMP_NTZ.

questions.q: Why does skipping the :: cast on refund_amount risk a wrong SUM() later?
options: An uncast VARIANT value can look numeric in a results grid but sort and compare as semi-structured, not a true NUMBER
SUM() only works on STRING columns in Snowflake
VARIANT columns cannot be included in a SELECT statement at all
Casting is only cosmetic and has no effect on aggregation
questions.explain: Skipping the cast is a common mistake — the field may display correctly but not behave as a true numeric type in aggregation or comparison.

questions.q: What happens when raw_payload:refund_amount::NUMBER(10,2) is applied to a row where the JSON has "refund_amount": null?
options: It becomes a true SQL NULL numeric value, same as an ordinary nullable column
It throws an error and the whole query fails
It becomes the literal text string "null"
It becomes zero
questions.explain: Snowflake's :field syntax returns SQL NULL automatically when a key is absent or its JSON value is null — no special-case handling needed.

questions.q: Why does this lesson say the preview SELECT matters more than a one-off exploration query?
options: It's the exact extraction logic Lesson 6's MERGE statement reuses field-for-field when writing the Stream's changes into the shared tables
Snowflake requires every table to have a matching preview query on file
It replaces the need for a CREATE TABLE statement entirely
It has no real bearing on later lessons
questions.explain: Proving the field names and casts here, against real data, means the later MERGE statement reuses a pattern already verified to work.
